provenance: Bounded clean-room isolation using the four existing public lalsimulation SimIMRSpinAlignedEOBModes datasets for 30+20 Msun, nonspinning, fstart=20 Hz, distance=100 Mpc. Public postpeak row 2 is treated as orbital phase and differentiated independently with fixed local polynomial orders 4/6/8. Clean Hamiltonian/flux/event, published base mode, and known-target NQC attachment are evaluated afresh in float64. No source waveform, public coefficient, time offset, phase offset, or residual-selected stencil is used.
primary_reference: Bohé et al., Improved effective-one-body model for coalescing nonprecessing binary black holes, arXiv:1611.03703 (equation context).

interpretation.phase_peak_vs_epoch: The returned phase-derivative peak follows the clean initial-origin omega event within a few 1e-3 M on every grid. It therefore does not reproduce the 0.01707037956 M common-epoch displacement: the epoch discrepancy is not encoded as a different returned phase peak.
interpretation.base_inspiral_mode_residual: The public complex mode contains its own NQC/attachment behavior over the returned support, so base-v-public residuals are NQC-confounded and do not by themselves identify a carrier discrepancy. The report also evaluates a fixed clean attachment-derived NQC factor before the match; this combined comparison is informative about the requested clean model contract but is not a public-NQC coefficient fit.
interpretation.runtime_recommendation: No additional runtime change is justified by this isolation. Keep the relative attachment grid arange(n)*dt/Msec and retain the public epoch as separate metadata; do not substitute -epoch for the clean event or fit a time/phase shift. A future change should target the clean carrier/factorized-mode contract and be validated independently.

limitations: The public phase row schema is used as the documented black-box observation from the paired wrapper; no LAL or PyCBC source is inspected.

The public mode includes its own NQC/attachment behavior. The base-mode comparison therefore cannot isolate the carrier; the separate NQC-corrected comparison applies only clean attachment-derived coefficients and never infers coefficients from public data.
The postmatch residual is available only where the clean attached output and public mode have the same relative output indices; it is raw complex subtraction with zero shifts.
Degree 4/6/8 phase stencils are predetermined numerical refinement diagnostics and are not selected by parity, residual, or agreement with the epoch.
